body.statement: Assume \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\ne\varnothing\). In the admissible specialization \(N=3,r=s=1\), \(\kappa_\star=1/\sqrt3\). For every nonempty endpoint stratum \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(1/\sqrt3)\), if \(T_0\ge\overline T\), the decision program \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{end}}\) satisfies \(\inf_{\vartheta\in\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(1/\sqrt3)}\Pr_\vartheta\{\beta\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{end}}\}\ge1-\alpha\) and, on every data realization, \(\operatorname{diam}_2(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{end}})\le\min\{2B,2\sqrt3\varepsilon_1\}\). Consequently, uniformly in \(T_1\ge1\), \(R_{\mathrm{or}}(1/\sqrt3)\asymp\min\{B,T_1^{-1/2}\}\), whereas \(R_{\mathrm{ad}}(1/\sqrt3)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(1/\sqrt3)\). The event \(\widehat h\ne h\) uses the reserved \(\alpha/2\) noncoverage budget and contributes no additive expected-diameter term because the displayed diameter bound is pathwise for every selected line.
body.justification: The endpoint result proves exactly when finite component classification can be charged to noncoverage rather than to expected diameter.
body.gap: EvansHansenStark2005 gives general confidence-set decision duality, but not this nuisance-profiled four-line panel experiment, its explicit finite-\(T_0\) error threshold, or its post-noise-only endpoint width.
body.consumer: It gives a transparent diagnostic for when a certified maximal loading margin makes margin-aware intervals much shorter than globally honest intervals.
